Russell Wilson. An American football quarterback who spent ten seasons with the Seattle Seahawks before moving to the Denver Broncos, earning a Super Bowl championship and becoming one of the most successful dual-threat quarterbacks of the 2010s. Known for his mobility, competitiveness, and ability to extend plays outside the pocket, he led the Seahawks to multiple playoff appearances and consistent division dominance. Drafted third round, seventy-fifth overall, in 2012 despite being a talented prospect, he became one of the greatest draft steals in modern NFL history. He won the Super Bowl XLVIII championship after the 2013 season with the Seahawks, leading the team to victory after a dominant defensive performance and winning the team's first championship in franchise history. He earned nine Pro Bowl selections from 2013 to 2021 and was selected to four All-Pro rosters, establishing himself as one of the decade's most consistent performers. Through his career he threw for fifty-four thousand eight hundred twenty-eight passing yards and four hundred eighteen touchdowns while rushing for over four thousand six hundred yards and fifty-one rushing touchdowns, demonstrating elite dual-threat capability. Known for his scrambling ability and capacity to extend plays outside the pocket, he created opportunities through improvisation and open-field athleticism. He led the Seahawks to multiple NFC West division titles and playoff appearances throughout the 2010s before being traded to the Denver Broncos in 2022 and subsequently moving to the Pittsburgh Steelers.
